condition: Pre-operative assessment — suspected obstructive sleep apnoea (STOP-Bang 8)
summary: 52-year-old man, BMI 42, loud snoring, witnessed apnoeas, daytime sleepiness, treated hypertension, neck 45 cm — STOP-Bang 8 — listed for laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Pre-operative assessment for planned gallbladder operation
inputs.hpi: Recurrent biliary colic, listed for laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Wife reports loud snoring and pauses in breathing at night; falls asleep watching television and once at traffic lights. Hypertension on amlodipine. Never had a sleep study. Walks slowly on the flat, breathless on one flight of stairs.

exam.general: BMI 42. Neck circumference 45 cm. Mallampati 3. HR 84, BP 148/92, RR 16, SpO2 95% on air, T 36.7°C.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Multiple mobile gallstones, gallbladder wall 2 mm, no pericholecystic fluid. CBD 4 mm. Liver normal.

comorbidities: Snoring with witnessed apnoeas (no sleep study)

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Pre-operative assessment — symptomatic gallstones; suspected OSA (STOP-Bang 8)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Symptomatic cholelithiasis for laparoscopic cholecystectomy. High risk of obstructive sleep apnoea: STOP-Bang 8/8. Class III obesity.

redFlags.note: Undiagnosed OSA raises the risk of post-operative respiratory events with opioids and sedation; it must be visible to the anaesthetist.

mustInclude.note: Risk-mitigation plan: anaesthetic awareness, opioid-sparing analgesia, post-operative monitoring; consider sleep study/CPAP where systemic disease is uncontrolled.

mustExclude.note: Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

guideline.name: SASM guideline — preoperative screening and assessment of adults with obstructive sleep apnoea
guideline.section: Screen with a validated tool (STOP-Bang); high-risk patients: consider further evaluation/CPAP where there is uncontrolled systemic disease or impaired gas exchange; otherwise proceed with risk-mitigation strategies (opioid-sparing analgesia, post-operative monitoring)
guideline.citation: Chung F, Memtsoudis SG, Ramachandran SK, et al. Anesth Analg. 2016;123:452–73.

guideline.name: ASA practice guidelines — perioperative management of patients with obstructive sleep apnoea
guideline.section: Preoperative identification; consider CPAP pre-operatively in severe OSA; minimise opioids; continuous monitoring after discharge from recovery while at increased risk
guideline.citation: American Society of Anesthesiologists Task Force on Perioperative Management of patients with OSA. Anesthesiology. 2014;120:268–86.

guideline.name: STOP-Bang questionnaire
guideline.section: Snoring, Tiredness, Observed apnoea, Pressure, BMI >35, Age >50, Neck circumference >40 cm, male Gender; 5–8 = high risk of moderate-severe OSA
guideline.citation: Chung F, Yegneswaran B, Liao P, et al. Anesthesiology. 2008;108:812–21 (risk bands: Chung F et al. Chest 2016;149:631–8).

guideline.name: ASA Physical Status Classification System
guideline.section: ASA I healthy; ASA II mild systemic disease; ASA III severe systemic disease; ASA IV severe systemic disease that is a constant threat to life; E suffix for emergency surgery
guideline.citation: American Society of Anesthesiologists. ASA Physical Status Classification System (last amended 13 December 2020).

rationale: Permutation: suspected OSA with class III obesity. Tests STOP-Bang suggestion, a visible OSA flag before anaesthesia and an OSA risk-mitigation plan.
